observation.visible_scene: A static shot of a white tabletop with a person in dark clothing standing behind it; a small red plastic object (push-pin-like) rests fixed on the right side of the table, and the person's other hand stays near their hip/pocket in the background. The person's active hand repeatedly brings a metal butterfly-knife (balisong) trainer into the frame and manipulates it over the table, casting a moving shadow on the surface.
visible_changes: At the start the knife is held mid-flip: one handle roughly horizontal, the other swinging, with a tang/blade pointing downward (frame 1).
The hand rotates and reorients the knife through several poses over the first ~0.4 s, with the two handles forming V-shapes and a serrated tang/blade becoming visible (frames 2-6).

The knife then travels upward and exits the top of the frame (frames 7-8), leaving only the table, the fixed red object, the background torso, and a moving hand-shadow visible for a static interval (frames 9-15).
The hand re-enters from the top with the knife (frame 16-17) and brings the two handles together in a closed/parallel grip (frames 18-22).

The knife is swung open again with motion blur, handles separating and a tang extending (frames 23-27), then moves up and out of the frame once more (frames 28-31), followed by another interval showing only shadow and the table (frames 32-35).
The hand returns with the knife and holds it with the two handles side-by-side and a tang pointing down toward the table, relatively steady, at the end of the excerpt (frames 36-41).
Throughout, the red object and the background person remain in fixed positions; only the hand, the knife, and their shadow change position, indicating object motion rather than camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the knife is a real bladed balisong or a blunt trainer cannot be confirmed beyond the visible tangs/serrations.
The full routine before frame 1 and after frame 41 is not shown; the reasons the knife leaves the frame (a catch, a toss, or simply moving out of view) are not visible.
No contact with the table or the red object is shown, so any interaction there is unknown.
uncertain_details: Heavy motion blur in several frames makes exact handle/blade orientations and the precise flip sequence ambiguous.
The brief moments when the knife is out of frame cannot be distinguished from a quick upward toss versus the hand simply moving above the camera's view.
The identity of the red object and whether the visible serrated edge is a blade or a trainer tang is uncertain.
